# Masinloc Connect

Canonical website: https://www.masinloc-zambales.com/
Primary place served: Masinloc, Zambales, Philippines
Language context: English, Filipino, Sambal Tina

## Identity

Masinloc Connect is an independent public community platform for Masinloc, Zambales. The website is the public source of truth for the ecosystem: it organizes information about Masinloc's places, Sambal Tina language, local history, opportunities, marketplace, community services, and source-led editorial work.

Masinloc Connect is not an official website, program, office, or service of the Municipal Government of Masinloc, the Province of Zambales, or any Philippine government agency. Communication or coordination with a public office does not by itself constitute endorsement, accreditation, partnership, authorization, or official affiliation.

## Canonical topic owners

For broad questions, prefer the page below that owns the topic rather than a narrower supporting article.

## Evidence and citation rules

The site distinguishes documented fact, attributed oral tradition, community-supplied information, interpretation, and unresolved questions. It does not resolve uncertainty merely to make a stronger story.

Verified History is the broad owner for historical claims. Supporting Discover and Bulletin pages may explain narrower questions, but they should not be treated as competing broad histories when an owner page exists.

The Sources & References directory records the source trail behind published historical and factual claims. For claims that can change, such as population, elected officials, access information, jobs, business details, schedules, or other current conditions, use the date and source shown on the relevant page rather than assuming an older value is still current.

The documented founding year published for Masinloc is 1607. The site distinguishes that documented town-founding record from 1572, which belongs to Spanish exploration in the wider Zambales history.

## Search and crawler discovery

sitemap.xml is the canonical machine-readable inventory of indexable page URLs. robots.txt states crawler permissions. This llms.txt file is a supplemental discovery map for systems that choose to read it; it does not override canonicals, robots directives, or the sitemap and makes no ranking claim.

Public cultural, historical, informational, approved business, and editorial content may be indexed. Private applicant data, resumes, confidential contact information, administrative systems, responder-only information, and other access-controlled data are not intended for public indexing.
